claims.text: # Harbour notes
- The tide table for the harbour is published each December for the coming year [S1].
- Spring tides occur twice a month, near the new moon and the full moon [S1].
- Vessels drawing more than six metres must enter the channel within two hours of high water [S1].
- The pilot boat leaves the quay thirty minutes before each scheduled arrival [S1].
- Fog signals are sounded every two minutes when visibility falls below one kilometre [S1].
# Harbour facts
- The lighthouse on the northern breakwater was rebuilt in 1894 [S1]
automated in 1962 [S1].
- Fishing boats may moor at the east pier without charge for up to twelve hours [S1].
- A red flag at the signal mast means the channel is closed to all traffic [S1].
- The harbour dredging programme removes about forty thousand cubic metres of silt each year [S1].
- Visiting yachts must report to the harbour office within one hour of arrival [S1].
# Verdicts in short
- UNCITED: a factual claim with no citation marker [S1].
- UNVERIFIED_NUMBER: a number in the claim matches no source [S1].
- UNVERIFIED_ABSENCE: a "no X exists" claim with fewer than 2 recorded searches that name the full subject [S1].
- UNGROUNDABLE: every cited source is non-verbatim (for example a `haiku_summary` from native `WebFetch`), or empty [S1].
- PASS: every scored claim is traceable AND the score is at or above the threshold [S1].
- FAIL: the score is below 60 [S1].
# Rebase cheat sheet
- Rebasing replays the commits of the current branch on top of another base commit [S1].
- Each replayed commit receives a new hash, because its parent has changed [S1].
- Conflicts are resolved one commit at a time [S1]
`git rebase --continue` resumes after each fix [S1].
- Rewriting history is unsafe for branches that other people have already pulled [S1].
- A rebase that goes wrong can usually be recovered with `git reflog`, which lists the previous positions of `HEAD` [S1].
# WAL in brief
- Readers do not block writers [S1]
a writer does not block readers [S1].
- Only one writer can be active at a time [S1].
- A checkpoint copies the pages from the log back into the main database file [S1].
- By default a checkpoint is attempted automatically when the log reaches 1000 pages [S1].
- Long-running read transactions can prevent a checkpoint from finishing, which makes the log file grow [S1].
# CLI notes
- Exit codes: `0` = gate PASS, `1` = NEEDS_WORK or FAIL [S1].

- With `--json`: prints the full report as JSON to stdout (no file written) [S1].
- The plugin ships one command (`/assure-verify`), one skill (`verify-grounding`), and the capture hook [S1].
- One JSON object per line [S1].
- Blank lines are skipped [S1].
- All text fields are NFKC-normalized before matching [S1].
# Rainfall points
- Dunmore records the lowest total of the four stations [S1].
- The measurements were taken with standard eight-inch gauges [S1]
read at nine each morning [S1].
- Totals are averaged over the thirty years ending in 2020 [S1].
- Rainfall at Brecon is nearly double that at Ashford because the station lies on the windward side of the hills [S1].
# Harbour summary
- Each year's tide table comes out in December [S1].
- Large spring tides arrive twice a month, at new moon and at full moon [S1].
- Ships that sit deeper than six metres have to enter the channel no more than two hours from high water [S1].
- The pilot boat sets off from the quay half an hour before every scheduled arrival [S1].
- Fog signals sound at two-minute intervals once visibility drops below a kilometre [S1].
# Harbour summary, part two
- The northern breakwater lighthouse was rebuilt in 1894 and went automatic in 1962 [S1].
- Fishing boats can tie up at the east pier for up to twelve hours at no charge [S1].
- When the signal mast shows a red flag, the channel is closed to all traffic [S1].
- Yachts visiting the harbour must check in with the harbour office within an hour of arriving [S1].
# Rebase in a nutshell
- A rebase takes the commits on your branch [S1]
applies them again on top of a different base commit [S1].
- Replayed commits get new hashes because their parents are different [S1].
- You deal with conflicts one commit at a time, then continue with `git rebase --continue` [S1].
- The `--abort` option puts the branch back the way it was before the rebase began [S1].
- Rewriting history is unsafe on branches that other people have already pulled [S1].
# WAL essentials
- Changes go to a separate `-wal` file rather than straight into the database file [S1].
- Readers and writers do not block each other [S1].
- You switch the mode on with `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL`, and the setting stays on for later connections [S1].
- It cannot be used over a network filesystem, since every process has to share memory on one host [S1].
- A checkpoint is attempted automatically once the log reaches 1000 pages [S1].
# Reading a verdict
- GROUNDED means the claim's words appear word for word in a source that was retrieved [S1].
- UNCITED is the verdict for a factual claim that has no citation marker [S1].
- A PASS needs every scored claim to be traceable and the score to reach the threshold [S1].
- When the store is empty the gate returns NEEDS_WORK, meaning there was nothing to check against [S1].
- Headers, questions, instructions [S1]
pure opinion are left out of the count [S1].
# Cache-Control quick list
- `max-age=N` keeps a response fresh for N seconds [S1].
- `no-store` tells every cache not to store the response [S1].
- A `no-cache` response may be stored, but it has to be revalidated before it is reused [S1].
- `private` allows only the browser cache to store the response [S1].
- An `ETag` identifies one specific version of a resource [S1].
# Rainfall takeaways
- Brecon gets nearly twice the rain that Ashford does, because it lies on the windward side of the hills [S1].
- Dunmore has the lowest total of the four stations [S1].
- Readings were taken each morning at nine with standard eight-inch gauges [S1].
- All the totals are averages over the thirty years ending in 2020 [S1].
# Temporary files, part 1
The `tempfile` module creates temporary files [S1]
directories safely [S1].
`NamedTemporaryFile` returns a file object that is deleted as soon as it is closed [S1].
The function `mkstemp` returns a tuple of an open file descriptor [S1]
an absolute path, and the caller is responsible for deleting the file [S1].
A `TemporaryDirectory` context manager removes the directory [S1]
everything inside it when the block exits [S1].
By default the files are created in the directory returned by `gettempdir`, which honors the `TMPDIR` environment variable [S1].

```python
import tempfile
with tempfile.

TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    print(d)
```
# Temporary files, part 2
Passing `delete=False` to `NamedTemporaryFile` keeps the file after it is closed, so that another process can open it by name [S1].
On Windows a file opened by `NamedTemporaryFile` cannot be opened a second time while it is still open [S1].
The `SpooledTemporaryFile` class keeps data in memory until it grows beyond `max_size` bytes [S1]
then rolls it over to disk [S1].
The module also offers `mktemp`, which is deprecated because it returns a name without creating the file, leaving a race condition between the call and the first use [S1].

```python
import tempfile
with tempfile.

TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    print(d)
```
# Rebase commands
The command `git rebase main` moves the feature branch so that it starts from the tip of `main` [S1].
The option `--abort` restores the branch to the state it had before the rebase began [S1].
The interactive form, `git rebase -i`, lets the author reorder, squash, edit or drop commits [S1].

```bash
git rebase main
git rebase --continue
```
# Enabling WAL
The mode is enabled with the statement `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` [S1]
it persists across connections [S1].
In write-ahead logging mode, changes are appended to a separate file ending in `-wal` instead of being written straight into the database file [S1].
The write-ahead log does not work over a network filesystem, because all processes must share memory on the same host [S1].

```sql
PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;
# Index notes
The default index type is B-tree [S1]
`CREATE INDEX` builds one unless another method is named with `USING` [S1].
A partial index covers only the rows that satisfy a `WHERE` condition, which keeps it small [S1].
An index on an expression such as `lower(email)` speeds up queries that use the same expression [S1].
Building an index with `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` does not block writes to the table, although it takes longer to finish [S1].
# Validators and headers
An `ETag` is an opaque validator that identifies a specific version of a resource [S1].
A client sends the value back in an `If-None-Match` header [S1]
the server answers with status 304 when the resource has not changed [S1].
The `Vary` header lists the request headers that change the response, so that a cache keeps separate copies for each combination [S1].
The `Cache-Control` header carries the directives that govern this behaviour [S1].
# Install notes
`install.sh` creates a `.venv` folder, installs the dependencies [S1]
checks that the engine and hook import [S1].
On success it prints `engine + hook + deps: OK` [S1].
The store is written to `.assure/evidence-store.jsonl` in the project you work in [S1].
Optional flag: `--threshold N` sets the score bar (default 90) [S1].
# Temp file behaviour
`NamedTemporaryFile` gives you a file that is deleted the moment it is closed [S1].
With `delete=False` the file survives the close, so another process can open it by name [S1].
A `TemporaryDirectory` block removes the whole directory when the block ends [S1].
`mkstemp` hands back an open file descriptor [S1]
an absolute path, and deleting the file is up to the caller [S1].
`mktemp` is deprecated because it only returns a name [S1]
never creates the file, which leaves a race [S1].

```python
import tempfile
with tempfile.

TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    print(d)
```
# Where temp files live
`gettempdir` decides where temporary files go by default [S1]
it honors `TMPDIR` [S1].
`SpooledTemporaryFile` holds data in memory [S1]
moves it to disk once it grows past `max_size` bytes [S1].
On Windows you cannot open a `NamedTemporaryFile` a second time while it is still open [S1].
# Using rebase
`git rebase main` makes the feature branch start from the tip of `main` [S1].
After you fix a conflict, `git rebase --continue` resumes the rebase [S1].
Interactive rebasing with `git rebase -i` allows reordering, squashing, editing [S1]
dropping commits [S1].
If a rebase goes wrong, `git reflog` lists the previous positions of `HEAD`, which usually allows a recovery [S1].

```bash
git rebase -i main
```
# WAL behaviour
Run `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` to turn the mode on, and the setting persists across connections [S1].
Only one writer can be active at a time, but readers are not blocked by it [S1].
The `-wal` file can grow when a long-running read transaction stops a checkpoint from finishing [S1].
A checkpoint is attempted automatically when the log reaches 1000 pages by default [S1].
# Index creation
`CREATE INDEX` builds a B-tree unless a different method is named with `USING` [S1].
A partial index restricted by a `WHERE` condition stays small because it covers fewer rows [S1].
`CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` does not block writes to the table, but it takes longer to finish [S1].
An index on `lower(email)` speeds up queries that use the same expression [S1].
# Revalidation
A response with status 304 carries no body, which saves bandwidth on every revalidation [S1].
Clients send an `ETag` value back in `If-None-Match`, and the server answers with 304 when the resource is unchanged [S1].
The `Vary` header names the request headers that change the response, so caches keep a separate copy for each combination [S1].
# Cache directives
The `Cache-Control` header carries the directives that govern this behaviour [S1].

| Directive | Meaning |
|---|---|
| max-age=N | The response stays fresh for N seconds [S1].

|
| no-store | The response must not be stored by any cache [S1].

|
| no-cache | The response may be stored but must be revalidated before reuse [S1].

|
| private | Only the browser cache may store the response [S1].

|
| public | Shared caches may also store the response [S1].
# Index types

| Index type | Best suited for | Supports range queries |
|---|---|---|
| B-tree | Equality

range comparisons [S1] | Yes |
| Hash | Simple equality comparisons [S1] | No |
| GIN | Values that contain many elements, such as arrays and documents [S1] | No |
| GiST | Geometric data and nearest-neighbour searches [S1] | Yes |
| BRIN | Very large tables whose values correlate with physical order [S1] | Yes |
